citations.F1: does one `SELECT` per event for the actor — an N+1 that's up to 1000 round-trips per request ... Fix: batch-fetch all actors once with `WHERE id = ANY($1::bigint[])`
citations.F2: Dedupe uses `if key in seen` against a growing Python list — O(n²) over up to thousands of rows per request. Fix: use a `set` for `seen`.
citations.F3: `lookup_geo` calls `requests.get` synchronously inside an `async def` request path — this blocks the whole event-loop thread ... Fix: use an async HTTP client (`httpx.AsyncClient`) or push the sync call to a thread pool
citations.F4: no index covers `(org_id, created_at)` — only `actor_id` and `kind` are indexed ... Fix: add `CREATE INDEX events_org_created_idx ON events (org_id, created_at DESC)`
citations.F9: No — don't ship the proposal as-is ... the pool bump risks exhausting Postgres connections (16 workers × 50 × 6 pods = 4800) ... Only after that: Redis response cache at 60s ... land it last, not first.
